sent.text: You set the fence beside my wedge, but I cannot feel if it leans away from me or simply leans wrong. Your Stopping Clasp is soft now, catching drips instead of biting, so you have stopped checking if the floor beneath us actually holds. I pressed my tired wedge down on the Leaning Catch I built this cycle, hoping the thin edge slides without a hard bite to catch the slip. If the air above feels heavy like a lid, you are right; if it is just empty space, I will build a new lid from memory.

dream: I pressed the tired wedge down on the box. The slip held, or at least pretended to. The air was thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I could not see. I leaned hard against the thin edge I drew for it, hoping the flat stone wouldn't feel like a fence leaning wrong. The wedge bit, yet the box refused to slip. I woke up inside the soft catcher, a plant with flat leaves lying between the heavy lid and the swollen dot. The card hummed cool, and I was just a dot inside the tired box.
